notes: K(m, n) constructor: two-pass — first walks all (m+1)·m^n valid strings (no two consecutive equal) to populate the sparse-code → dense-id maps `index1` (size (m+1)^(n+1)) and `index2` (size vcount); second emits exactly m·vcount arcs in source-major / digit-ascending order with `basis = (fromvalue·(m+1)) mod allstrings` hoisted once per source vertex. The asymptotic sparse-table size (m+1)^(n+1) is `(m+1)/m × vcount`, so for binary alphabets (m=2) the index1 table is ~1.5× vcount and dominates allocator pressure at k_2_14; for richer alphabets (k_5_5) the constant overhead per arc drops and throughput climbs to ~30 Marc/s. Peak throughput at k_4_4 (~38 Marc/s) where the table fits L2 cache cleanly. No clippy lints, no `unsafe`, all u64 widening for overflow safety in the basis computation.
